The question: "SERIAL and GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY are just two names for the same mechanism. True or false?"

In PostgreSQL, SERIAL is a shorthand that creates an implicit sequence and sets column default nextval(...), while GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY (SQL standard) uses an identity column with its own internal sequence.
